rules.title: San Diego Residential Tenant Protections (just cause, relocation assistance, buyouts, retaliation)
rules.requirement: Landlords may not end a covered tenancy without an at-fault or no-fault just cause stated in the notice. For no-fault terminations they must pay or waive 2 months' rent as relocation assistance (3 months if the tenant is a senior 62+ or disabled), give 30/60 days' notice, and offer re-rental if the unit is re-offered within 5 years. Buyout agreements are regulated and retaliation is prohibited.
rules.key_value: Relocation assistance: 2 months' rent (3 months if senior/disabled) for no-fault terminations
citation_aliases: San Diego Mun. Code ch. 9, art. 8, div. 7
rules.quoted_span: A landlord shall not terminate a tenancy without just cause. For purposes of this Division, just cause includes at-fault just cause and no-fault just cause
rules.effective_date_note: Division as retitled/expanded by O-21647 N.S. effective 2023-06-24; amended by O-21769 N.S. effective 2024-03-28. Legal Aid fact sheet (D077) also states 2023-06-24.
rules.coverage_conditions: Tenancies longer than 30 days (not fixed terms of 3 months or less) in residential rental property in San Diego.
rules.exemptions: Transient hotels, short-term rentals, deed-restricted or subsidized affordable housing (not Section 8), mobilehomes under MRL, nonprofit hospital/religious/care facilities, dormitories, shared-facility rentals with live-in landlord, owner-occupied single-family residence, owner-occupied duplex, housing with certificate of occupancy within previous 15 years, and separately alienable property (e.g., condos) owned by non-REIT/corporate landlords with written notice.
rules.penalty: Civil action for injunctive relief and damages including punitive; wrongful eviction damages of at least 3x actual economic damages; at least 3x relocation assistance owed; attorney's fees; notices void for noncompliance; City enforcement.
rules.interaction: Rights are in addition to state and federal rights; consistent with Cal. Civ. Code § 1946.2 but provides greater relocation assistance (2-3 months vs. 1 month).
rules.conflict_note: Local rule governs over the state Tenant Protection Act just-cause rule where both cover a unit.

unverifiable_exemptions: separately alienable property owned by non-corporate landlord with notice
dormitories, care facilities, nonprofit transitional housing

rules.title: Prohibition of Anti-Competitive Automated Rent Price-Fixing
rules.requirement: Landlords may not use algorithmic software that analyzes nonpublic competitor data to set rents or occupancy levels, and vendors may not sell or license such software to landlords. Tenants can sue for injunctions, damages, or civil penalties up to $1,000 per violation, plus attorney's fees; each month and property is a separate violation.
rules.key_value: ban on algorithmic devices using nonpublic competitor data; civil penalties up to $1,000 per violation
citation_aliases: San Diego Mun. Code ch. 9, art. 8, div. 11
Prohibition of Anti-Competitive Automated Rent Price-Fixing Ordinance
rules.quoted_span: It is unlawful for a landlord to use an algorithmic device to set rental rates or occupancy levels for residential rental property
rules.effective_date_note: Official draft (D076) says effective the thirtieth day after final passage with blank dates; law-firm alerts (D002, D037) state effective June 2025. Exact day not available.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to landlords and residential rental property in the City of San Diego.
rules.exemptions: Excludes software publishing reports from aggregated historical nonpublic data more than 90 days old or public information that does not recommend future rents; software used to set rents or income limits under affordable housing program guidelines.
rules.penalty: Injunctive relief, damages, or civil penalties up to $1,000 per violation; each month and each property a separate violation; prevailing tenant recovers costs and attorney's fees.
rules.conflict_note: Official text provided is the draft ordinance with blank adoption date; enactment and June 2025 effective month rely on secondary sources (Morgan Lewis, Aug 2026). Now being litigated in Keller v. UDR Inc. (S.D. Cal.).

unverifiable_exemptions: software used for affordable housing program rent/income limits

no_rule_findings.finding: No San Diego local rent-increase cap appears in the documents; the city's own tenant-protection notice points tenants to the state cap, so the state Tenant Protection Act governs.
no_rule_findings.quoted_span: California law limits the amount your rent can be increased. See California Civil Code section 1947.12 for more information.

parsed.notes: Merged the two just-cause candidates (official code D073 plus Legal Aid fact sheet) and the three algorithmic-pricing candidates. Nothing in the provided documents covers San Diego security deposits, application fees or screening restrictions. D075's page was only a code table of contents, so I added no rule for those categories. A source-of-income division may exist in the San Diego code, but I couldn't verify it.
